clue.text: Unrefined performance art hyped somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A critic sniffs at a piece of over-promoted performance art as rather crude.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and unpolished, so the word is a synonym of crude or unsophisticated.

clue.text: 14's letter delivered on round

definitions.note: the answer to 14 across, LASSO, used as a verb: to catch by throwing a loop around

indicators.note: a letter delivered is spoken, so we want the sound of the letter, written out as a word

parts.note: the reference 14 also points to the fourteenth letter of the alphabet, N
a circle is a round shape

explanation.surface: Reads like a note about a postman's round and a letter for somebody called 14.
explanation.walkthrough: '14' does double duty: it is the cross-reference to 14 across (LASSO) for the definition, and also points to the fourteenth letter of the alphabet. In a down entry, 'on' means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso a steer is to throw a rope loop around it, i.e. surround it completely.

clue.text: On River Test, current site vacated to develop plants again?

parts.note: RE means 'on' or 'concerning', as in a letter heading
the Indus is a major river of Pakistan
a trial is a test
I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: a site vacated has its contents emptied out, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Plans to put industry back on the banks of the River Test, a Hampshire chalk stream, once a site is cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Test' looks like the Hampshire river but splits into two separate pieces. 'Plants' are factories, not flowers, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial plants are factories, so building factories again is to bring industry back to an area.

clue.text: Elder has indeed gone dressed up for exercise with special pants

parts.note: hath is the older form of has
ay is an old word for yes, indeed

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for 'gone' is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ago means gone by, in the past

explanation.surface: An older person has really gone and got dressed up for a workout in special trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pants' are not trousers but breaths: this form of yoga uses special breathing exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatha yoga is a physical yoga discipline combining postures with controlled breathing techniques.

clue.text: Sandy recalled certain module thwarting student festivity

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the assembled letters are read backwards
thwarting is read as lying athwart, across the middle of the student festivity word

parts.note: a rag is a British student charity festival
the lunar module is one particular module, from the Apollo missions

explanation.surface: Sandy remembered that one course unit got in the way of the students' party.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag (week) is a British student fundraising carnival; the lunar module flew the Apollo moon landings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand consists of small grains, so a sandy texture is a granular one.

clue.text: Approaching due north: wild hog

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of 'due north' running out of control into a new order

parts.note: to hog is to monopolise, as to corner a market

explanation.surface: A compass reading points straight at a wild boar.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just round the corner is near at hand, imminent, about to arrive.

clue.text: Specialised biscuit with hard filling

indicators.note: the letter for hard is the filling put inside the biscuit

parts.note: a Nice is a coconut-flavoured biscuit popular in Britain
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A specialist biscuit with a hard centre.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nice biscuit (said like the French city) is a sugar-topped coconut biscuit sold in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche product serves a narrow specialist market, so the word works as an adjective for specialised.

clue.text: Vertigo Ray endured on vacation between capes

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light

indicators.note: between places the emptied word in the gap separating the two capes

parts.note: head and ness are both words for a cape or headland

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of endured

explanation.surface: Somebody called Ray suffered dizziness while holidaying between two headlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Both cape words are British place-name elements for a headland, as in Beachy Head and Orford Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a dizzy, swimming sensation, the feeling of faintness that the compound noun describes.

clue.text: One capital in Asia, dry, unusually hot

definitions.text: One capital in Asia, dry, unusually hot

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters being put together in an unusual order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: capital means the first, upper-case letter of the word Asia

parts.note: H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A description of a Middle Eastern city: arid and exceptionally warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the Saudi capital is notoriously dry and hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital city of Saudi Arabia, on the Asian continent, with a desert climate.

clue.text: Unerring marine maybe scans phone for vital text

parts.note: dead means exact or unerring, as in dead accurate or a dead shot
marine means of the sea
one scrolls through a phone screen when scanning it

explanation.surface: A sharpshooting marine checks his phone for an important message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unerring marine' suggests a soldier, but 'marine' is the adjective for of the sea, and unerring is as in a dead shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Jewish manuscripts found at Qumran are of key importance to biblical scholarship.

clue.text: Bit tense reporting rank booze

parts.note: a coin is a bit, as in a threepenny bit
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: reporting means the word for rank is as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: a row is a rank or line

explanation.surface: A slightly tense account of foul-smelling alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective (smelly) describing the booze, but it is a row; spoken, ROW gives the French ending -REAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange liqueur, a brand of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Frank's opposite number gradually rising through banks in City

indicators.note: through puts one word passing inside the other, between the banks
the banks of a word are its outer letters, here those of City

parts.note: your age is a number that goes up slowly year by year

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank faces a rival whose figures creep up through the City banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name; it is the adjective for candid. 'Number gradually rising' is a cryptic hint for AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cagey means being guarded and secretive, the reverse of open and candid.

clue.text: Send off wine that valentine receives

parts.note: red is red wine
a valentine is sent as a card

explanation.surface: Posting off a bottle of wine for one's sweetheart on Valentine's Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send off' looks like posting a gift; it is the referee's action.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a referee shows a player the red card to dismiss them from the pitch.

clue.text: Proper tango old rocker performed with partner

parts.note: due means proper or fitting, as in due care
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a Teddy boy, or Ted, was a 1950s British rock and roll fan

explanation.surface: An aged rock-and-roller danced a correct tango with his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: A Ted (Teddy boy) was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress devoted to rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is a piece for two players, so to have duetted is to have sung or played as a pair.

clue.text: The Spanish like this feller on ranch?

parts.note: las is a Spanish word for the, used before feminine plural nouns
so means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: Spaniards approve of a cowboy-type fellow out on the ranch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' looks like slang for fellow; it is something that fells, bringing cattle to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's rope with a running noose is used to catch and bring down cattle.

clue.text: The Spread Eagle mean to install communication system

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so these letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle

indicators.note: a mean is a middle value, so take the central letter of install

explanation.surface: A pub called The Spread Eagle intends to put in a new phone network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Spread Eagle' reads as a pub name. The middle of INSTALL is T, joined with THE and ERNE in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethernet is the standard wired networking technology linking computers in a local area network.

clue.text: Fishing gear around trailer seat affected position of stability

indicators.note: around puts the fishing gear on either side of the other letters

parts.note: a rod is fishing tackle
an ad is a trailer, a promotional advertisement

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of seat are changed around

explanation.surface: Fishing tackle stowed around a car trailer seat upset its balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailer' looks like a towed vehicle; it is a film advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadstead is a sheltered stretch of water near a shore where ships can ride safely at anchor.

clue.text: Shelter with debris, occasionally drinking

parts.note: and means together with

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only every other letter of debris

parts.note: on means drinking, as in on the bottle

explanation.surface: A shelter full of rubble where someone occasionally takes a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of 'debris' give ERS. An Anderson shelter was a British back-garden air-raid shelter of World War II.
explanation.definitionFit: The corrugated-steel air-raid refuge issued to British households in WWII bore this name.

clue.text: Period dummy I used in short illusion

indicators.note: used in means placed inside, here the shortened illusion word
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a trick is an illusion
an ass is a dummy, a fool

explanation.surface: A ventriloquist's dummy said it was briefly used in a magic trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period' is the definition, meaning a span of geological time rather than a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The Triassic is a geological era, the first age of the Mesozoic, when dinosaurs appeared.

clue.text: Charge hardware?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put an extra charge on a bill
second meaning: a piece of extra equipment attached to a computer

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'hardware' needs the computer sense, as an extra plugged-in device.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both an extra fee tacked on and an accessory that extends a computer system.

clue.text: Plant succulents, passing time in borders of arboreta

indicators.note: in places the shortened succulents word inside the borders
the borders of a word are its first and last letters
passing means losing the letter T, the time abbreviation

parts.note: cacti are succulent plants

explanation.surface: Instructions to plant succulents over time around the edges of arboretums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb; it is the noun definition, and 'time' gives its usual abbreviation to be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a tree or shrub, the wattle, so it is a botanical name for a plant.

clue.text: Disheartened, Carol departs leaving blighted garden bloomer

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, keeping the outer letters of Carol
leaving says that the letter for departs comes out of garden
blighted means ruined, so the remaining letters are disarranged

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Carol, downcast, abandons a garden ruined by blight, flowers and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a flower; it is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a mistake, and a clanger is an embarrassing, noisy blunder.

clue.text: Raise spirit for a start

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; the phrase is 'from the get-go'

parts.note: to get money is to raise it
go means energy or spirit, get-up-and-go

explanation.surface: Lifting one's spirits to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: From the get-go is an American idiom meaning from the very beginning or outset.

clue.text: Leftovers on retiring is expected

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is is written backwards

parts.note: due means expected, as in the train is due

explanation.surface: Remarks on retirement, which is anticipated.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains after the rest has gone, so it is a collective word for remnants.

clue.text: Minor rider passing leading pair

indicators.note: passing means going without, and the leading pair are the first two letters

parts.note: a cyclist rides a bike

explanation.surface: A minor cyclist overtakes the two front-runners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' looks like a young person; it is the adjective for second-rate, as in a C-list celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: The C-list ranks below the A and B lists, so a C-list figure is of lesser, third-tier fame.

clue.text: Separately, one European enters drunk, being his own boss?

indicators.note: enters says the letters go inside the word for drunk
separately says the two letters go in at different places

parts.note: legless is British slang for very drunk
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A drunk European staggers in alone, behaving as if he were the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Legless is British slang for paralytic drunk. I goes after the L and E after the G, in separate places.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal lord; with no lord above you, you answer to nobody, hence the question mark.

clue.text: What was that river by Alabama pub?

parts.note: AL is the US postal abbreviation for Alabama
eh is said when you didn't catch something
the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, among others in England

explanation.surface: Puzzled by a river in Alabama, someone asks where the pub is.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is an old word for a tavern, a place selling beer to drink on the premises.

clue.text: Price of surplus back numbers

parts.note: odd means extra or left over, as in the odd one

indicators.note: back means the word for numbers is read in reverse

explanation.surface: The cost of excess back issues of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back numbers' looks like old magazine issues; 'back' is the reversal of NOS.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, an odds-on price means the stake is greater than the potential winnings, a favourite's quote.
